title: Effect of high-dose vitamin D supplementation on peripheral arterial calcification: secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial
authors: Billington EO, Burt LA, Plett R, Rose MS, Boyd SK, Hanley DA
population: Calgary Vitamin D Study: community-dwelling adults aged 55 to 70 years with serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D 30 to 125 nmol/L (mean 78.9 nmol/L)
funder: The full text was not accessible. Registry: lead sponsor University of Calgary; collaborator Pure North S'Energy Foundation. The primary trial report states that funding came from Pure North S'Energy Foundation, which had no role in design, conduct, analysis or publication.
inKindSupport: Primary report: vitamin D3 drops provided by Ddrops Canada.
result: Vitamin D3 400 (n=105), 4000 (n=96) or 10,000 IU/day (n=101) for 3 years; tibial artery calcification measured by HR-pQCT at baseline, 6, 12, 24 and 36 months. At baseline 85 participants (28%) had calcification, mean 2.8 mg hydroxyapatite (95% CI 1.7 to 3.9), which increased by 0.020 mgHA per month (0.012 to 0.029) with no treatment-group effect (P=0.645 for interaction); no participant developed new arterial calcification.
